planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring or early fall into moist, humus-rich soil; a touch of afternoon shade intensifies the bronze foliage tone compared with full-shade siting.

directions: Set divisions into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial shade, giving a few hours of morning or dappled sun to deepen the bronze-red leaf color without scorching it. Pumpkin Spice (US Plant Patent PP29,925) is a Walters Gardens introduction bred by Hans Hansen from a complex Heuchera line carrying 'Southern Comfort' ancestry crossed onto Tiarella 'Jade Peacock,' so it shrugs off summer heat and humidity far better than many foamy bells, and its lobed, mahogany-veined foliage holds color from late spring into early summer before mellowing toward green. Cream flowers rise on dark red stems above the clump in early summer, drawing bees. Lift and divide crowns every three to four years once they begin to heave above the soil line.

planting.note: Plant bare-root crowns or container stock in spring or early fall into humus-rich, consistently moist soil in part to full shade; set the crown at the same depth it grew in the pot.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in part to full shade, where this Proven Winners Shadowland introduction forms a broad specimen clump of heart-shaped, powdery-blue leaves rimmed in a wide gold margin. The margin actually opens apple-green and shifts to gold as the season progresses, and where the blue center meets the gold edge a faint lighter watermark halo appears, a trait breeders prize as a rare genetic marker in hosta foliage. White flowers open on scapes above the leaves in early summer, but the plant earns its spot in the border on foliage alone. Mulch to keep roots cool and moist, and watch for slug damage on the soft spring growth.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into free-draining, humus-rich soil in partial shade; good sun-scorch resistance lets it tolerate brighter sites than most lungworts.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, free-draining soil in partial shade, where this Terra Nova Nurseries introduction forms a dense, low mound of sharply pointed, gray-green leaves finished with cream-silver edges and a heavily veiled, frosted surface. Terra Nova markets it as an updated take on their earlier 'Raspberry Splash,' keeping that plant's easy nature while refining the leaf pattern. Bright coral-red flowers open in early spring before the leaf canopy fully expands, then get tidily hidden as new foliage fills in. Divide congested clumps after bloom every three to four years, and keep soil from drying out during summer to prevent leaf scorch.
